title: Local business group
titleCn: 本地商业团体LBG给新移民的求职建议

paragraphs.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions eleven to fourteen.

Good morning, everyone. My name's John Baldwin, and I'm the chairman of this city's LBG, the local business group. In the past few months, we've been delighted to welcome many different nationalities with impressive language skills who have arrived to settle here in Markstone. The LBG has a list of the names and addresses of various businesses in this area, and we want to target those of you with specialist backgrounds. At the moment, we're spoiled for radiologists, but we're faced with a severe shortage of pharmacists. In fact, if you visit any of the job centers in this city or go online, you'll see advertisements for several vacancies in this field. Though until recently, it was psychologists who were in short supply. So bearing all this in mind, we have advice which I hope you'll find useful.

Many of you are extremely well qualified. However, most professional job applicants need to submit their original diplomas or certificates, whatever their background. If you haven't brought these with you, then get them sent to you as soon as possible. What's more, you will need a signature and stamp on the documents from someone in authority at the institution where you took the examinations. Also, once in your possession, make photocopies of them for safekeeping.

Now, when you're submitting a job application to a potential employer, we suggest you post your application by recorded delivery just in case things go astray. It costs a bit extra, but the receipt gives you peace of mind. It's not advisable to hand things in personally. And remember, most employers will require an email address. Markstone has plenty of Internet cafes, so use these facilities if necessary.

The LBG is keen to compile as much useful information as possible based on your experience. So my colleagues and I will be better prepared to support people in dealing with these formalities than we have been in the past. We've designed a register, and although it's not compulsory, we'd like you to add your name, address, and profession to this register before you leave today. I'll be around to answer any questions.
Before you hear the rest of the talk, you have some time to look at questions fifteen to twenty.
Now listen and answer questions fifteen to twenty.

Finally, the LBG's map is specifically targeted at people like yourselves. This was enclosed with your invitation to today's meeting. We are sitting in LBG's office marked at the bottom left-hand side of your map. It's on one side of the city square, which has a fountain in the middle. On the north side of the square is Markstone's pedestrian thoroughfare, which is completely traffic free.
If you need a translation service, you'll find it in the large building accessed directly from the pedestrian thoroughfare to the west of Broad Street.
Okay. Now to find the bank, walk along Broad Street from the pedestrian thoroughfare, keeping the park on your right, and you'll find it on the corner with Markstone Avenue.
If you need to discuss money at any stage, even a small loan, then I recommend talking to the manager, who is extremely helpful.

Now, to find the community center, turn right at the north end of Broad Street into Markstone Avenue, and in the same block as the park, you'll see it situated between two other buildings. You'll find advice on housing and health services, and it's open from ten till five daily.

If you need to travel outside the city for a job interview, look for the Dial-A-Car kiosk. It's on the north side of Markstone Avenue, opposite the junction with New Road. It's equipped with a free telephone connection to Markstone's Dial-A-Car service. The company is offering half-price fares on all journeys if you explain that you are on our LBG register. That's a very generous discount.
The post office is on New Road, roughly halfway between Markstone Avenue and the pedestrian thoroughfare.

Finally, there's a modest cafe called Welcome. It's run by the LBG and is open each evening. If you start from the city square and keep on walking along the pedestrian thoroughfare in an easterly direction, it's just after the junction with New Road. Drop in for free tea
